observation_summary: The StringUtils.replaceEach method throws a NullPointerException when an element in the replacementList array is null, because the code attempts to call .length() on it without checking for null.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding a conditional check (if (searchList[i] == null || replacementList[i] == null) continue;) to validate the input data before performing operations that would cause a NullPointerException. This is a classic case of missing input validation/guard logic.
evidence_used: The stack trace shows a NullPointerException at StringUtils.java:3676.
Line 3676 in the buggy code is: int greater = replacementList[i].length() - searchList[i].length();
The fix adds a null check for both searchList[i] and replacementList[i] before accessing their length properties.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The core logic of the replacement algorithm is correct; the failure is specifically due to a lack of validation for null inputs, which is the definition of a Checking defect.
